brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full bases (piece:0,0,0 to piece:3,0,0), each with a hex-bin-third-drain bin filled with soil and planted (prop:1 to prop:4).

requirements.requirement: A water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: run:run-1 is an irrigation run at level 0 that enters at edge 3 of cell (0,0) and passes through cells (1,0), (2,0) and (3,0). It is a single straight run, so every cell still takes a third-depth bin.

The run passes under all four bins, which have drain holes. The configurator checks fit only, though: it does not test that the pipe is watertight or that water actually reaches each bin. The far end in cell (3,0) is closed by a solid end cap (cap:3,0,0;*;330). I can't see from the configurator whether that cap seals the pipe end. Nothing in the build models how the pipe lets water out to each cell.

finish.summary:
I built a planter of four full bases in a straight row, cells (0,0) to (3,0) at level 0. One irrigation pipe run (run:run-1) goes in through the outer face of cell (0,0) and runs straight through the bases of all four cells. Because the pipe passes through each base, each cell can only take a third-depth bin, so each holds a drained third-depth bin filled with soil and planted. I added solid end caps on the open faces and bolted the joints. check_build reports no rule issues, the mesh check is clear and there are no prop warnings. The build is 29 printed parts, about 1813 g of filament and about 2678 minutes of printing.

One thing went wrong along the way. My first plan_build placed the bases in a cluster, and the pipe did not reach the starting cell (0,0). I removed that layout and placed the straight row with apply, because plan_build would not take a new plan after the removal. The pipe and bins were also added with apply.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
